stem: Which statement best distinguishes a node from an internode?
choices: A node is an attachment or growth point; an internode is the stem segment between adjacent nodes
A node is a root tip; an internode is a leaf blade
A node is a mature flower; an internode is a seed coat
A node is a calendar stage; an internode is a cultivar category
rationale: Nodes organize leaves, branches, buds, and reproductive structures along the shoot, while internodes are the stem segments separating adjacent nodes.
